title: Where Artifact logic is ambiguous the Executor Agent must do nothing and force a token holder vote
content:
A.1.14.2.7.2.1 sets the boundary of automated execution: "An Executor Agent must not implement Omni Document logic where it requires a subjective judgment call or use of discretion. Accordingly, Omni Documents must set out clear, specific and deterministic instructions for updating the relevant Agent Artifact."

A.1.14.2.7.2.1.1 supplies both the test and the default. The test is intersubjective: an Executor "may not update a Prime Agent Artifact if the relevant logic requires a significant degree of discretion, such that **reasonable people may differ** on how to interpret and implement the action." The default is fail-closed: "If there is ambiguity as to whether an Agent Artifact authorizes an Executor Agent to directly update the Artifact, the Executor Agent must err on the side of not making any changes," and "the Agent must enact the change to the Artifact through a Root Edit process."

A.1.14.3.4.2 imposes the mirror-image duty on the other party: Prime Agent Artifacts "must include highly detailed and deterministic instructions" that Executors can "implement... without ambiguity or the use of discretion." Determinism is the Prime's drafting obligation; refusing to guess is the Executor's.

The design insight is that ambiguity is routed rather than resolved. An Executor confronted with unclear instructions has no interpretive authority to fall back on — it escalates to the only body that does, the token holders. That prevents the operational layer from accumulating de facto legislative power through repeated interpretation, which is how administrators in most systems come to shape the rules they execute. The cost is that vague drafting produces stalls, and the incentive to draft precisely is that imprecision converts routine work into a governance vote.
description: Executors may not implement logic requiring subjective judgment; if reasonable people could differ, or if authorization is unclear, the change must go through the Root Edit process instead.
